title: Three habits for faster code reviews

scenes.headline: Slow reviews are a habit problem
scenes.narration: Your pull request has been sitting for two days. The code is fine. The review process is what's slow. Three small habits can fix that.

scenes.headline: Habit one: keep changes small
scenes.narration: Reviewers put off big diffs because they take real focus. A change someone can read in ten minutes gets reviewed between meetings, not next week.
scenes.body: Aim for one idea per pull request, and split refactors from behavior changes.

scenes.headline: Habit two: review yourself first
scenes.narration: Read your own diff before anyone else does. You'll catch the stray debug line, the unclear name, the missing test. Every nit you fix is a round trip you save.
scenes.body: Open the diff in the review tool, not your editor, and read it like a stranger would.

scenes.headline: Habit three: write a useful description
scenes.narration: Tell the reviewer what to expect before they open a single file. Context up front means fewer questions in the comments and faster approvals.

scenes.headline: A description template you can reuse
scenes.narration: Here's a template. Paste it into your repository's pull request settings so everyone starts from the same shape.

code.text:
## What
One sentence on the change.

## Why
The problem this solves.

## Testing
How I verified it.

## Review notes
Start with src/api/handler.ts

scenes.headline: Try one habit this week
scenes.narration: Pick one of the three and use it on your next pull request. Small diffs, a self-review, a clear description. Your teammates will notice the difference.
scenes.body: Faster reviews are a team skill, and you can start today.
